description.value: You attack with a weapon you're wielding or with an unarmed attack, targeting one creature within your reach (for a melee attack) or within range (for a ranged attack). Roll the attack roll for the weapon or unarmed attack you're using, and compare the result to the target creature's AC to determine the effect.
You move up to your Speed.
You carefully move 5 feet. Unlike most types of movement, Stepping doesn't trigger reactions that are triggered by movement.
You position your shield to protect yourself. When you have Raised a Shield, you gain its listed circumstance bonus to AC and saving throws until the start of your next turn.

Trigger: While you have your shield raised, you would take physical damage. You snap your shield in place to ward off a blow. Your shield prevents you from taking an amount of damage up to the shield's Hardness.

You scan an area for signs of creatures or objects. If you're looking for creatures, choose a 30-foot cone or a 15-foot burst within line of sight. You might detect undetected creatures or hidden objects.
You attempt a skill check to try to remember a bit of knowledge regarding a topic related to that skill. The GM determines the DC, and they can modify it based on how obscure the knowledge is.

Trigger: An ally is about to use an action that requires a skill check or attack roll. You position yourself to help your ally perform a common task. You use the relevant skill or perform the relevant task. If your check meets the DC, your ally gains a +2 circumstance bonus; if you critically succeed, they gain +3.
